title: Corners: Voices on Change
target_audience: Readers interested in contemporary social and cultural issues
Individuals curious about community, identity, and change
Fans of essay collections and anthologies
Those engaged with Irish and UK literature
General readers seeking fresh perspectives on society
core_themes: Marginality and 'corners' as physical and metaphorical spaces
primary_purpose: To give a platform to a diverse range of writers, artists, and thinkers to reflect on moments of change—personal, communal, political, and cultural—exploring 'corners' as spaces of transition, resistance, and transformation.

structure_format.narrative_style: Varied; includes personal essays, memoir, reportage, and creative nonfiction
structure_format.organization: Anthology: individual essays/works by multiple contributors, each with unique perspective
features: Blend of established and emerging voices
Exploration of recurrent motifs (corners, boundaries, edges)

key_concepts_lessons: Change often happens on the margins, not the center.
Personal histories intertwine with larger societal shifts.
Spaces seen as peripheral or forgotten can become sources of resilience and creativity.
The act of giving voice to diverse experience is itself transformative.
Identity and community are in constant negotiation and flux.
Listening to those in 'corners' of society broadens collective understanding.
notable_features: Curated by award-winning writer Lucy Caldwell
Features a range of prominent and emerging writers (including Kayo Chingonyi, Jan Carson, Sinéad Gleeson, among others)
Multi-genre anthology with essays, memoir, reflections, and reportage
Focus on contemporary issues facing Ireland and the UK, with global resonances
Exploration of both physical and metaphorical 'corners'
cultural_historical_context: Published as part of a collaborative literary project at a time of significant social and political change in Ireland, the UK, and globally—post-pandemic, post-Brexit—engaging questions of identity, belonging, and the meaning of community in rapidly changing times.
reception_impact: Praised by critics for its breadth of voices and depth of reflection
Celebrated in literary circles as a timely and necessary anthology
Has spurred conversations about representation, marginality, and change in contemporary society
comparable_titles: Winter Papers (edited by Kevin Barry and Olivia Smith)
The Good Immigrant (edited by Nikesh Shukla)
Being Various: New Irish Short Stories (edited by Lucy Caldwell)
Common People: An Anthology of Working-Class Writers (edited by Kit de Waal)
